content.title: What is Searching?
content.description: Searching is the process of finding whether a particular element exists in an array and determining its position if found.

content.content: Imagine you are looking for a specific book in a library or a contact in your phone. The process of locating that item is called searching. In Data Structures, searching helps us find required data quickly and efficiently.

content.title: Why Searching Matters
content.content: Searching is one of the most frequently performed operations in software applications, databases, search engines, and operating systems.
Linear Search is the simplest searching technique. We start from the first element and compare each element with the target value until we find a match or reach the end of the array.

content.title: Best Use Case
content.content: Linear Search works well for small or unsorted arrays.
Binary Search is a much faster searching technique that works only on sorted arrays. Instead of checking every element, it repeatedly divides the search space into two halves.

content.title: Key Requirement
content.description: Binary Search requires the array to be sorted. If the array is unsorted, Binary Search cannot be applied directly.

content.title: Binary Search Workflow
steps: If target is smaller, search left half
If target is larger, search right half

content.title: Real-Life Analogy
content.content: Finding a name in an unsorted notebook is like Linear Search—you check every page. Finding a word in a dictionary is like Binary Search—you open near the middle and eliminate half the pages instantly.

content.title: Did You Know?
content.content: Google Search, database indexing, and many large-scale systems use advanced searching techniques built upon the principles of Binary Search.

items.question: Can Binary Search be used on unsorted arrays?
items.answer: No. The array must be sorted before Binary Search can be applied.

items.question: Why is Binary Search faster?
items.answer: Because it eliminates half of the remaining elements after each comparison.

items.question: What happens if the element is not found?
items.answer: The search continues until the search space becomes empty.

content.title: Interview Insight
content.description: Whenever you see a sorted array in a coding interview, think about whether Binary Search can reduce the time complexity.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Searching is used to locate an element in an array.
Linear Search checks elements one by one.
Binary Search works only on sorted arrays.
Binary Search complexity is O(log n).
Binary Search is generally faster than Linear Search.
